משׁך 625 משׁה
2. a part, portion, as measured out,
Lev. 7, 35; see the root no. 2.
מָשְׁחָה f. 1. Inf. of the root מָשַׁח to
anoint; see above.
2. a part, portion, Ex. 40, 15. Num.
18, 8; see מִשְׁחָה no. 2.
מַשְׁחִית pr. part. Hiph. (r. שָׁחַת) plur.
מַשְׁחִיתִים, destroying, which destroys;
hence Subst.
1. a destroyer, desolater, Jer. 22, 7.
Spec. in war, collect. הַמַּשְׁחִית the de-
stroyers, troops in ambush rushing forth
to destroy, 1 Sam. 13, 17. 14, 15.
2. destruction, Ex. 12, 13. 2 Chr. 20,
21, 36 [31] חָרָשֵׁי מַשְׁחִית artificers of de-
struction, skilled to destroy. Spec. of
arms and weapons for destroying, Is. 54,
16; also of snares, traps, Jer. 5, 26.—So
אִישׁ מַשְׁחִית a man of destruction, a de-
stroyer, Prov. 28, 24. But בַּעַל מַשְׁ׳ Prov.
18, 9 is one who brings destruction on
himself, a waster, prodigal.—Also הַר
הַמַּשְׁ׳ the mount of destruction; spoken
of the mount of Olives or its southern
part, on account of the idol-worship set
up there by Solomon, 2 K. 23, 13, Vulg.
mons offensionis. Also of Babylon for
the like reason, Jer. 51, 25.
מִשְׁחָר m. i. q. שַׁחַר, the dawn, aurora,
Ps. 110, 3; see in art. טַל. R.שָׁחַר I.
מַשְׁחֵת i. q. מַשְׁחִית no. 1, destruction,
once Ez. 9, 1. R. שָׁחַת.
מִשְׁחָת m. (r. שָׁחַת) constr. מִשְׁחַת,
destruction, defacement; for concr. de-
stroyed, disfigured, once Is. 52, 14.
מָשְׁחָת m. (r. שָׁחַת) c. suff. מָשְׁחָתָם,
destruction, i. e. something destroyed or
disfigured, i. q. defacement, blemish, Lev.
מִשְׁטֹח m. (r. שָׁטַח) Ez. 47, 10, constr.
מִשְׁטַח Ez. 26, 5. 14, a spreading, i. e.
place for spreading.
מִשְׁטָר m. c. suff. מִשְׁטָרוֹ, dominion,
empire, influence. Job 38 33 אִם תָּשִׂים
מִשְׁטָרוֹ בָּאָרֶץ dost thou assign the domi-
nion (of the heavens) over the earth?
R. שָׁטַר.
מֶשִׁי m. Ez. 16, 13, in pause מֶשִׁי v. 10,
according to the Heb. intpp. silk, a gar-
ment of silk. Sept. τρίχαπτον i. e. ac-
cording to Hesychius τὸ βομβύκινον
ὕφασμα. Jerome, ‘a garment so fine as
to seem equal to the finest hair.’ From
the root (מָשָׁה to draw) we can derive
no other sense than ‘something finely
drawn,’ e. g. a fine thread, stuff com-
posed of fine threads.
מְשִׁי, see מוֹשִׁי.
מְשֵׁיזַבְאֵל (delivered of God, r. שֵׁיזַב
Chald.) Meshezabeel, pr. n. m. Neh. 3, 4.
מָשִׁיחַ m. (r. מָשַׁח) constr. מְשִׁיחַ, c.
suff. מְשִׁיחִי.
1. Adj. verbal pass. χριστός, ointed,
anointed, of a shield 2 Sam. 1, 21; מָשִׁיחַ
נָגִיד the anointed prince i. e. Cyrus,
Dan. 9, 25; הַכֹּהֵן הַמָּשִׁיחַ the anointed
priest, the high priest, Lev. 4, 3. 5. 16.
2. Subst. ὁ Χριστός, the Messiah, the
anointed, the prince consecrated by unc-
tion, Dan. 9, 26.—More fully מְשִׁיחַ יְיָ
the anointed of Jehovah, Sept. ὁ Χριστὸς
Κυρίου, a name of honour given to the
Jewish kings, as being consecrated by
anointing, and therefore most sacred,
of Cyrus king of Persia Is. 45, 1. Not
used of the great Deliverer predicted
by the prophets; although his usual
name (מְשִׁיחָא ὁ Μεσσίας) among the
later Jews and in the N. T. is drawn
from passages like Ps. 2, 2. Dan. 9, 26;
comp. John 1, 42. 4, 25. Buxtorf. Lex.
Chald. art. מְשִׁיחָא. [Yet Ps. 2, 2 is re-
ferred directly to the Saviour in Acts 4,
26 sq.—R.] Plur. the anointed of Jeho-
vah, spoken of the patriarchs, Ps. 105,
* מָשַׁךְ, fut. יִמְשֹׁךְ; imper. מְשֹׁךְ,
plur. מִשְׁכוּ Ex. 12, 21, and מָשְׁכוּ Ez.
1. to draw, to drag, Arab. مسك id.

Golius and Freytag this signification is
wanting. Kindred is מָשָׁה.—With an
acc. of pers. to draw any one to a person
or place, with בְּ or אֶל of place, Judg. 4,
7. Ps. 10, 9; comp. Cant. 1, 4. Contra,

line_status.note: The vowel under the mem is a qamets (T-shaped mark, matching the qamets under the chet), not a hiriq dot; this is the second entry מָשְׁחָה, distinct from מִשְ�ְׁחָה treated above.
The mem carries a single dot (hiriq, מִ), not qamets as in A; the printed line also has a space before the semicolon ("8 ;"), matching B.

The print has a visible space before the semicolon ("3 ;", as in B) but "R." is set tight against שָׁחַר with no space (as in A); neither reading has both spacings right. Hebrew pointing matches both.

Both Hebrew words carry patach (a horizontal stroke, not a single chirik dot) under the mem; the first word has tsere (two dots) under the chet, and the second has chirik + yod. Reading A matches; Reading B's chirik under mem and patach under chet are wrong.

Under the initial mem in both the headword and the suffixed form the print shows a horizontal bar with a dot beneath (qamets), not a single hireq dot; so מָשְׁחָת / מָשְׁחָתָם as in Reading B (consistent with Lev. 22:25).
